committed: before any spike code, any oracle output and any measurement existed

groups.common: what every verdict needs: the kernel stays lazy and costs the budgets nothing
groups.inversion: the two-layer core-radius inversion, its moment-of-inertia check and its refusals
groups.oblateness: the Darwin-Radau flattening from rotation, its refusals and its uncertainty

order: a common check that is not a pass (or a pass under a ruling): C
else an oblateness check that is not a pass: C
else an inversion check that is not a pass: B (oblateness only)
decision.rule: a check that was not measured is never a pass; a check recorded as pass-under-ruling counts as a pass and its row carries the ruling; 'inversion passes alone' is C because Appendix C names no such slice

oblateness.qConvention: q = omega^2 a^3 / (G M), equatorial radius a, f = (a - b) / a

checks.bound: two-layer core radius and mass: kernel against the oracle's brentq root and quad integral on 1,500 seeded points: relative error at most 1e-12 (core radius 1e-10)
moment-of-inertia factor against scipy quad on the same 1,500 points to 1e-9; rho_c = rho_m gives 0.4 exactly
Earth's core radius from the in-situ layer means, mass and radius against the published core-mantle boundary (3,480 km) within 2.0 percent (a closure test, stated)
Mars's core radius against 1,830 km within 5.0 percent (a closure test, stated)

seeded ensemble of 1,000 Earth-like and 1,000 Mars-like synthetic bodies, truth densities from the table's stated spread, M and R with 0.01 percent noise: the stated 1-sigma interval on the core radius covers the truth at a rate in [0.63, 0.73] and the 2-sigma interval at least 0.92, in each cluster

the moment-of-inertia factor predicted from the inverted structure within 10 percent of the published factor (Earth 0.3307, Mars 0.364), and a homogeneous body (0.4) ruled out by each published factor by more than 10 times its stated error
at least 20 hostile or out-of-domain inputs each refused with a named code and no number
Darwin-Radau forward and inverse against the oracle's closed form to 1e-12 on 1,000 seeded points; the homogeneous limit returns f = 5 q / 4; the round trip f to C to f returns the input

for 200 seeded two-layer profiles and the n = 1 polytrope: Darwin-Radau flattening from the exact moment of inertia against the oracle's first-order Clairaut flattening, at q = 0.01: relative error in f at most 3.0 percent; the oracle must pass its self-tests first (homogeneous: eta 0, factor 0.4, f = 5q/4; polytrope factor (2/3)(1 - 6/pi^2) to 1e-8)
Earth's flattening from the published moment (0.3307), GM, the equatorial radius and the sidereal period against 1/298.257 within 2.0 percent
Jupiter's flattening from the published moment (0.264), GM, the equatorial radius (71,492 km) and the System III period against f = 0.06487 (IAU radii 71,492 and 66,854 km) within 10.0 percent
Earth's flattening from the two-layer model's own moment (the inversion's) and the rotation against the published value within 10.0 percent

seeded ensemble of 1,000 two-layer profiles at q = 0.0035 (moment known to 0.002, q to 1 percent): the stated 1-sigma interval on f (propagated error plus a model term of 1 percent of f) covers the oracle's first-order Clairaut flattening at a rate in [0.60, 0.76]
